newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.

text.p: FISCHER CONFIDENT REPUBLICAN CONVENTION WILL GO AHEAD
Deputy Prime Minister Tim Fischer says republicism is a second-order issue but he's confident the Government will set up a people's convention and a plebiscite on the republic.
Federal Cabinet's expected to canvass the matter today at its first meeting of the year.
Mr Fischer says the Coalition's priority issues are boosting exports and ensuring job creation across the economy.
It's been speculated the Coalition's seeking to delay the convention, with some in Government ranks also concerned that electing delegates would be unworkable.
New South Wales Liberal Opposition leader Peter Collins has called on the Government to move quickly, saying Australians expect the Prime Minister to act.
FIRES STILL OUT OF CONTROL IN VICTORIA
Firefighters are still battling to control five blazes, sparked by lightning, in Victoria's National Parks.

The Department of Natural Resources and Environment says seven other fires are contained, and 27 smaller fires are under control. The Department says the main fires are in the far north west of the state, with the largest burning on a 12 kilometre front in the Big Desert Wilderness Park.
He says it's anticipated all the fires will be under control by tomorrow morning.
DEMOCRATS UNLIKELY TO BACK CHANGES TO ABC CHARTER
The Australian Democrats have signalled they are unlikely to support any changes to the ABC's charter as a result of the Mansfield Review.
The Mansfield review recommends changes to the ABC charter to commit the organisation to news, current affairs, regional, youth and children's services.
Democrats Spokeswoman, Vicki Bourne, says they will assume that the public interest is most likely to be protected if they vote against any changes to the charter advocated by the Government.
Senator Bourne says there is growing evidence of the Coalition's long standing determination to damage the ABC.

She's angered by the revelation of a 1991 letter from the Coalition's former Communications spokesman, Warwick Smith, in which he calls for a major scaling down of the ABC and a A$50 million funding cut.
ANTHRAX POSES VIRTUALLY NO RISK TO PEOPLE - MINISTER
Victoria's Acting Agriculture Minister, Bill McGrath, says there's only a very minimal risk to milk consumers from an outbreak of anthrax near Shepparton.
Fifteen dairy cows have died and two properties are quarantined as a result of the outbreak, detected on Sunday.
Milk taken from the infected herd has been disposed of and Mr McGrath says the risk to humans is virtually nil.
He says milk companies can trace milk coming into the system and will ensure contaminated milk doesn't go into the manufacturing process or liquid milk chain.
SHARK ATTACK VICTIM STILL IN HOSPITAL
Doctors say a man mauled by a shark in North Queensland last weekend, will probably remain in hospital for at least another day.
Victorian Derek Burrows is in Mackay Base Hospital with deep cuts to the legs, after being mauled by a two-metre shark, while honeymooning in the Whitsundays.
Mr Burrows hopes to be discharged by Thursday, when the couple will return to Victoria.
BID TO EXTRADITE BELL MOVES FORWARD
Federal Attorney General Darryl Williams says New South Wales authorities have now provided the material necessary for the application for the extradition of alleged paedophile Philip Bell.
Mr Williams says he's signed the formal extradition request which will accompany the documentation required to support the application for extradition.
A spokesman for Mr Williams says the application includes documentation relating to the at least 215 counts New South Wales police wish to speak to Mr Bell about.
The application is being forwarded through diplomatic channels to reach South Africa in time for Mr Bell's reappearance in court on February the fourth.
The spokesman says the complete application has arrived well inside the 45 days required under South African extradition law. - - - -
NORTHERN TERRITORY ATTORNEY WANTS UNION JACK REMOVED
Northern Territory Attorney-General Denis Burke says it's time Australia stopped thinking about becoming a republic and did something positive towards the change.
Mr Burke has followed Australian Of The Year Peter Doherty in suggesting that removing the Union Jack from the Australian flag would be a positive step in a move to a republic.
He says he thinks the Prime Minister is dragging his feet on the republic issue, adding that he thinks an overhwleming majority of Australians want the issue progressed.
STOLLE WINS PLACE IN DAVIS CUP TEAM
Sandon Stolle has won a place in Australia's Davis Cup team for the tie against France starting on the 7th of February at White City.

Stolle will be joined by Pat Rafter, Mark Woodforde and Todd Woodbridge. This weekend in the leadup to the tie, Scott Draper, Richard Fromberg and Micheal Tebbutt have a chance to force their way into the team with a series of matches at White City.
Mark Philippoussis and Jason Stoltenburg were not considered because of injury.
TAB EYES INTERNET BETTING
TAB chiefs from around Australia will discuss Internet betting this afternoon as part of a two-day conference on betting and new technology.
The conference, which is being held in Hobart, will also examine the pros and cons of privatisation, and commission deductions taken from TAB turnover.

The general manager of the Tasmanian TAB, Tony Morse, says the agencies are keen to move with new forms of interactive betting. He says new technology will soon allow punters to lay bets through their television. The conference ends today.
-- Reuters Sydney newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
